req.title: Task deletion persists
req.statement: The system shall remove deleted rows so subsequent GET returns 404 for that id.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that deleting a task must persist: the row is removed from the database so a subsequent GET returns 404. We need: (1) a positive test confirming DELETE returns 204 and GET then returns 404 for the same id; (2) a negative test confirming DELETE on a non-existent id returns 404; (3) a boundary test confirming the state transition is durable (the deleted task does not reappear in the list). Additional tests cover: double-delete idempotency, deletion of a pre-loaded row, and exact status-code assertions to kill comparison-operator mutations.

tests.name: test_delete_existing_task_returns_204_and_subsequent_get_returns_404
preconditions: A new task is created via POST to obtain a known id
actions: POST /tasks/ to create a task and capture its id
expected: DELETE returns HTTP 204 with no body
GET returns HTTP 404 confirming persistence of deletion
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app

client = TestClient(app)

def test_delete_existing_task_returns_204_and_subsequent_get_returns_404():
    create_resp = client.post("/tasks/", json={"title": "Temp task", "description": "to delete", "completed": False})
    assert create_resp.status_code == 201
    task_id = create_resp.json()["id"]

    del_resp = client.delete(f"/tasks/{task_id}")
    assert del_resp.status_code == 204
    assert del_resp.content == b""

    get_resp = client.get(f"/tasks/{task_id}")
    assert get_resp.status_code == 404
    detail = get_resp.json()["detail"]
    assert str(task_id) in detail

tests.name: test_deleted_task_absent_from_list
actions: GET /tasks/ again and verify count decreased by exactly 1
Verify id 1 is not present in the returned list
expected: List count after deletion equals baseline count minus 1 (19)
Id 1 does not appear in the list response
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app

client = TestClient(app)

def test_deleted_task_absent_from_list():
    before_resp = client.get("/tasks/", params={"limit": 1000})
    assert before_resp.status_code == 200
    before_ids = [t["id"] for t in before_resp.json()]
    assert 1 in before_ids
    before_count = len(before_ids)

    del_resp = client.delete("/tasks/1")
    assert del_resp.status_code == 204

    after_resp = client.get("/tasks/", params={"limit": 1000})
    assert after_resp.status_code == 200
    after_ids = [t["id"] for t in after_resp.json()]
    assert len(after_ids) == before_count - 1
    assert 1 not in after_ids

tests.name: test_double_delete_second_returns_404
preconditions: A new task is created and then deleted once
expected: Second DELETE returns HTTP 404 (row no longer exists)
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app

client = TestClient(app)

def test_double_delete_second_returns_404():
    create_resp = client.post("/tasks/", json={"title": "Double delete task", "completed": False})
    assert create_resp.status_code == 201
    task_id = create_resp.json()["id"]

    first_del = client.delete(f"/tasks/{task_id}")
    assert first_del.status_code == 204

    second_del = client.delete(f"/tasks/{task_id}")
    assert second_del.status_code == 404
    body = second_del.json()
    assert "detail" in body
    assert str(task_id) in body["detail"]

tests.name: test_delete_preloaded_row_20_persists
preconditions: Id 20 exists with title 'Reply to emails'
actions: GET /tasks/20 to confirm it exists before deletion
GET /tasks/20 to confirm it is gone
expected: Initial GET returns HTTP 200 with id 20
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app

client = TestClient(app)

def test_delete_preloaded_row_20_persists():
    pre_get = client.get("/tasks/20")
    assert pre_get.status_code == 200
    assert pre_get.json()["id"] == 20
    assert pre_get.json()["title"] == "Reply to emails"

    del_resp = client.delete("/tasks/20")
    assert del_resp.status_code == 204
    assert del_resp.content == b""

    post_get = client.get("/tasks/20")
    assert post_get.status_code == 404

tests.name: test_delete_boundary_id_zero_returns_404_or_422
preconditions: Id 0 does not exist (ids start at 1)
actions: DELETE /tasks/0 where 0 is below the minimum valid id
expected: DELETE returns HTTP 404 (not found) or HTTP 422 (validation error) — never 204
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app

client = TestClient(app)

def test_delete_boundary_id_zero_returns_404_or_422():
    del_resp = client.delete("/tasks/0")
    assert del_resp.status_code != 204
    assert del_resp.status_code in (404, 422)

tests.name: test_delete_does_not_affect_other_tasks
actions: GET /tasks/3 to confirm sibling row is unaffected
expected: GET /tasks/3 returns HTTP 200 with id 3 and title 'Submit expense report'
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app

client = TestClient(app)

def test_delete_does_not_affect_other_tasks():
    del_resp = client.delete("/tasks/2")
    assert del_resp.status_code == 204

    sibling_resp = client.get("/tasks/3")
    assert sibling_resp.status_code == 200
    sibling = sibling_resp.json()
    assert sibling["id"] == 3
    assert sibling["title"] == "Submit expense report"
    assert sibling["completed"] == True
